Killing Floor 2 is a wave-based, co op shooter. It is truly an incredible game and well worth re-writing a review for.
This is the game that truly got me into gaming at all. It drove me to upgrade from Intel HD graphics to an 560 ti, to finally building a new beast machine from scratch.
There are just so many things that this game got right. First, the gun play is fantastic. I've never seen better gun animations and models, barring perhaps the Battlefield franchise which is reknown for it's realism in weaponry. The BLAST of a double barrel shotgun or the whistling of an RPG rocket are all done to perfection.
Next, the co op is where this game truly shines. While a very fun experience playing solo, when you play with 5 other people all with different weapons shredding, exploding, blasting, and slicing through zeds (this game's "zombies) it feels very epic. Especially to the pounding metal which I already listened to before even getting this game.
Probably one of my favorite aspects of this game is the developers (which can't be said for a lot of games). Tripwire has been so loyal to this game and I can't really give them enough praise for all the continued support they give to Killing Floor 2. Every few months out comes a new weapon, map, or game mode, so don't feel that if you buy this game you are buying a dead end, dying product (quite the opposite).
If you have the rig to handle it, I highly suggest turning all settings up to maximum for this game (including Nvidia flex). While a massive performance hitter, the gore is just ridiculous. I've never seen any other game that has such explosive and in-your-face gore, besides Doom 2016. It makes it pretty satisfying to blast zeds when they fall into pieces and blood flows into a puddle at your feet. Yikes.
In summary, you can't go wrong with this game, especially on sale. As you can see I've put way too much time into this game and it will only go up as Tripwire adds more content. You can make or play on custom maps, jam to metal music, and slay monsters with your friends. It's awesome!!!

Dead Space is a wonderful game combining many genres, third person shooter, survival, action, and horror, all into on. While some games fail when trying to do too much, Dead Space is able to do all of these parts well and deliver a satisfying experience from start to finish.
Dead Space progresses very nicely from start to finish. The story is intriguing and, while horrifying space creatures is nothing new, presents a well rounded and detail/lore filled experience that took some thought to follow. The opening sequence leads very nicely right into the action, immediately making you want to find out just what happened to that ship.
As far as firefights go, this game offers some intense sequences. Whenever I overcame a hoard of enemies I felt like a badass, but I always hoped that an engagement like that wouldn't happen again. This may be what Dead Space does best: present you in an environment that makes you uncomfortable, leave you feeling exposed at all times, and give you just enough to get the job done if you do it right and think on your feet.
That being said, I found the biggest flaws in the game to also center around the combat situations. While there are plenty of action sequences in the game, it is not as smooth as other action games, which is of course fine as this isn't the initial purpose. However, some sequences and enemies felt cheap to me when you meet them. The enemies are varied, challenging, and interesting as a whole, but some sequences are downright frustrating. Often this happens when an objective is not fully clear or your purpose is not adequately explained. I don't expect a game to hold my hand, but when it isn't clear what that button you just pressed does, but swarms of enemies come out of the vents, it can become exhasperating. Fortunately, this doesn't happen too often.
The progression system in Dead Space is very good and rewarding. You can build your loadout to your playstyle and upgrade equipment to suit your strengths. Dead Space offers a variety of weapons to use and tactics to implement to keep battles fresh and fun.
I would definitely recommend Dead Space, even though it is a few years old. It is still a great game, and at a discount during Christmas or summer for $5 simply can't be missed.

An overambitious, overcomplicated, disappointing entry in the Arkham series.
The combat, which was so fluid and satisfying in Arkham City, now has too many bells and whistles thrown in. The controls, which were much refined from Arkham Asylum to Arkham City, seem to have devolved again into more fiddly and annoying (seriously, who can switch to Alt+number keys in the middle of a combo??). Combat controls for the Batmobile ensure you'll have cramped fingers within a few seconds, as you're either holding down "W" to accellerate or the RMB to stay in 'battle mode' during a battle - apparently toggles are out of fashion.
The story takes itself far too seriously, unable to decide if the tone should be dark psychological horror (the oh, GODS so annoying unskippable Joker crap), or confident and inspiring tale of victory against the odds. The twists are telegraphed from a mile away, we're forced to once again sit through the illusion of choice as Batman makes mind-numbingly stupid decisions throughout, and never learns a damn thing.
There are good things in here. The refinements to Predator combat, especially the varied use of the disruptor weapon and the 'fear' takedowns, are a joy to play, but you don't get to play with them anything like enough to put up with the rest of the crap.
Avoid this bloated, self-indulgent misery-fest, and just play through Arkham City a few more times.

Oddly, if you keep pressing the aim button and "C" or "F" (how you activate the stasis/kinesis)... then it eventually starts working.  Once you get it working, it will work consistently for the rest of your gameplay.
And again, the strange thing is... once it starts working, it continues to work for the rest of your gameplay(unless you exit the game)
This bug had me VERY confused the first time I played this, because the instructions on how to use the Stasis left me feeling like I didn't understand how to use it (it *is* HOLD aim then press C)... and the instructions I felt did not clearly show that (it should have said "hold" next to the mouse/aim button).
One more small design detail needs to be corrected in this game.  Every transition from every level is smoothly done, *except* for the transition from level 11 to level 12.
I hope they fix this in future updates.
Graphics: 10/10
Looks great.... I hate rating graphics because there is a lot more to design than graphics... and in 20 years people will complain at how dated it looks.... but for now they are great.
Fear Factor: 2/10
I was told this was one of the scariest games ever made, so in that respect it is a huge disappointment.
Stuff jumps out at you, but it happens so often that it never surprises you.  The game is really easy, and there is some tension, but not the type of tension that makes you afraid.  The designers did not know how to build up suspense.
In terms of scariness... this game doesnt even hold a candle to games like Amnesia or Silent Hill. Even Phantasmagoria from 1995 scared me more than Dead Space.
Sound: 8/10
Voice acting is perfect.... It has a good soundtrack, good sound effects, good weapon noises...
Where the problem with the sound comes in, is that they overdid it.  Sometimes less is more and the constant whispering in your ear fails to make you feel fear... whereas, if they took their sound effects and used them more stragegically in a more suspensful way... this would be much higher.
Story: 8/10
Decent story.  I am not into spoilers so I will leave it at that.
Game Design: 9.5/10
The interfaces look great, the pop-up videos look great and work great, the audio files are well acted, the character movement is natural looking... I would give this a 10/10.. BUT.... there was ONE bug that I came across... in the room where that one guy is giving a speech on the hologram in the middle of the room.... if you go into the next room and pull up your holo-display item interface (maybe it was I played a video, I cant remember)... but when you do this... the video that is looping in the other room becomes visible THROUGH the wall... so that bug needs to be addressed.
Fun Factor: 10/10
The story is good, the gameplay is good, the sound is good, the design is good... but the game is just damn fun.
I love upgrading the weapons and only having some of the weapons.
My only complaint here is that when you replay the game, you cannot switch to a harder mode.
Replay Value: 8/10
What I think would be nice would be to be able to replay the game on after playing it on medium(you dont seem to be able to change this if you play through it a second time).. I think to make it quasi-challenging, they should allow you to keep 50% of the total sale value(ie 25% of the purchase value for the armor) of all your weapons and armor purchases if you keep the setting the same or 25% of their total sale value(ie 12.5% of the purchase value for the armor) if you change the setting from easy to normal or normal to hard on the second play.... or nothing if you change the difficulty from "easy" to "hard".
The game was too easy and letting you keep everything AND giving you nodes AND cash AND a better suit kind of makes the replay-value sort of lame.
So...
OVERALL SCORE: 9/10
If you are looking for a VERY fun game that is gory and morbid, but not too scary... then this is for you.
***NON-SPOILER TIPS & QUICK-GUIDE FOR FIRST TIME PLAYERS***
If you are reading this review before playing the game, then here is a non-spoiler recommendation.
First things first:
This game is easy enough on "normal"...
Don't bother playing it on "easy" unless this is one of your first ever 3rd person shooters.
Second of all:
Always make an effort to upgrade your armor first before purchasing weapon upgrades, but don't sell power nodes to do so.
Thirdly:
Always use a power node to open those special rooms... This is not a trick, the reward is always greater than the cost.
Fourth(but most helpful):
Do not buy all 7 weapons, you only really need to use 3 weapons in the entire game(the first weapon is free).  Although the first weapon is free, and you only need 3 weapons... you should buy 3 specific weapons instead of just 2.  You should buy the 4th one because the ammo from it is very valuable for selling.
Ammo for weapons does not appear unless you have the weapons in your inventory, so do not bother buying the 6 weapons for purchase(the plasma cutter is free) because that money would be better spent buying power nodes to upgrade your weapons.
The weapons you should choose for the first time playing are(in this particular order):
1) The Plasma Cutter (Most versatile weapon in the game, good in every situation... upgrade every useful node on this gun first)
2) The Line Gun (very powerful, but not good for small enemies)
3) The Pulse Rifle (lots of ammo, good for swarms of small enemies)
4) The Contact Beam (very powerful, but don't bother with using it until you upgrade all your other weapons first... mostly I say choose this because selling its ammo will give you 4,000 credits in the store.  Start using it after you upgrade all the other weapons first.)
Fifth:
You can sell most of your stasis refils, because refil stations are abundant in every level....
Except there are NONE in level 10 and 11, so you only really *need* them in those levels.
Lastly, (concerning upgrading):
Do not even bother buying new weapons until you first get every *useful* node in the weapons you have.  The reason being, the game only spawns ammo from the guns you carry.... and if you are following my advice and upgrading only one weapon at a time, then it just makes sense to have a stockpile of ammo for your most poweful weapon(which will be the Plasma Cutter first).
Note that there is no special reward for upgrading every node in a weapon, so only bother with the useful nodes and most efficient paths.
Try to upgrade your damage nodes first, this will make your ammo more effective.
Also, a useful trick for getting extra ammo is to upgrade your capacity nodes when your weapon is empty or near empty and you will get a free reload(NICE!).
This same trick works with upgrading your HP on your suit, if you have low HP and upgrade your suit... your HP completely refils.
And least usefully, if you have no stasis energy, it also works when you upgrade your stasis capacity.
*Extra Info*
The weapons usefulness in order are:
1) Plasma Cutter
2&3) Line Gun or Pulse Rifle
4) Contact Beam
5&6) Force Gun or Ripper
7) Flamethrower

Shadowrun returns for me was an interesting game to begin with. Combat feels a little shallow at times and the different skills didn't really stand up usually there being only 1-2 max 3 good options to use. Also the saving system is a complete dork. Not to forget that there's a possibility to create your own campaigns and play community created content as well which add greatly to the game length. That is if there is anything great created which I honestly just don't know... maybe baby!

TL;DR: I love this game, I've spent more hours than I care to admit on it, and I would definitely recommend it to anyone who likes challenging, and fast-paced gameplay. Don't get if your computer doesn't have too much RAM. 10 bucks is definitely worth it.
And now for the review
Rogue-Likes are a very dear friend to me. I like them because of their very difficult nature and the simple elegance of the gameplay. They are also very unforgivingly difficult, and will not hesitate to squat all over your dreams and take a long, yet aggressive dump on all your hopes and dreams, but I digress. I would not exactly call Risk of Rain a full on Rogue-Like.
There are 6 stages on every playthrough. For the first 4 levels of the game, it is randomly picked between 2 stages per level. The fifth is the same level no matter what. The maps stay relatively similar, barring a few details that make it different. These details can be memorized, and it makes the game a little predictable. The Final stage (stage 6) is the same level, and the same design every time you play through. Long story short, the maps are kind of random, but not really. No matter though.
The real unique part of each playthrough is the items and the artifacts. The Artifacts change the way the game is played, like having the enemies explode on death, hurting everyone (including you) around them. another locks one of your four skills every minute, but decreases your other cooldowns by a half. My personal favorite is the one that makes you deal 5x damage, but start at 1/10 health. Using a mix of artifacts, your games can turn from "Eh, I'm used to this" back to the way you felt when you first started getting used to the game.
The items buff your character, cause different effects to happen, and change the way the combat flows, depending on what you get. After you get enough items, there is nary a thing that can stop you. You can even play the first 5 stages over and over again before progressing to the final stage just to get the most god-like character ever. The power-creep in this game is very real. When it gets to the point that we're firing 2 missles on every shot, speeding through levels like Usain Bolt on amphetamines, vaporizing anything stupid enough to get near you, and also firing off a plasma lazer that destroys everything on screen every 25 seconds of so, the game starts to get a very "Prototype-y" feel of being too overpowered. And I love it.
Problem with getting too overpowered? This game is merciless on the cooling unit in my laptop. When the in-game clock is passing by at 1 second every 3 actual seconds, you have about 2 minutes to finish the game before your computer crashes. Changing the quality doesn't seem to help. All this is at a very god-like point in the game.
It is extremely difficult. I had about 10 playthroughs before I could pass the 2nd stage, and about 15 in-game hours before I beat it for the first time. but my, was that moment just the sweetest dang thing.
I love this game, and the game developers are doing a very good job of keeping it updated. I have spent about 150 hours on this game, and I regret none of it. 10 dollars is a very fair price for what you get, and I would recommend this to anyone who loves a challenge in their games.
Comparisons with Portal are inevitable, but Antichamber is a lovely, unique experience that combines taxing-but-not-frustrating puzzles with charm and wisdom. Fun.

Growing up in 90s and one of my very first PC games was "Fallout", you can imagine how excited I am when I received "Shadowrun Returns" from my friend as a gift in Steam. This game is everything we ever loved about role playing turn based strategy PC game which we grow up with. Here is a quick review of "Shadowrun Returns"
Simple yet richly detailed iso-metric view. Every background, every characters are so much detailed. Although, this type of graphics seems outdated in today 3D standards, it is very refreshing and enjoyable to look at the whole area, or looking at the amazing drawing of the character potriat.
Weak in overall. It does captures the environment of neo-futuristics sound but it could be improved. There is no memorable music or sound in the whole game except for the title music. Even so, everything is minimal.
This is what captures the player. The Story of Shadowrun Returns! Without spoiling anything - You start out alone in the apartment where you received a video call from your "Best Buddy". Turns out that its a dead video which is triggered when the person died. Now its up to you to uncover the bottom of your friend's murder (and receive $ in doing so). You will feel like you are reading a great noval and the story drives you keep playing the game one area after another.
This is the heart of the "Shadowrun Returns". If you are fan of Turn Based strategy game like original "Fallout", you will feel that this is everything you wished for in "Fallout 3". You will need a lot of strategy to think, move, shot, or get into cover. You use magic or gun or just plain melee to wack the heck out of enemy. You will have two action points as simple as that is. There is no calculation of how many action point you need to do something. You either move and shot or shot twice in one turn. All up to you. You will wish you want to have more encounters just to have a little more fan with gameplay before moving on with story line. On top of that, you have wide arrays of custormization for your characters - from choosing race to your profession. You gain karma points from making choices in game which can be used to upgrade your character skills.
Highly recommended to all hardcore player and fan of Turn Based Strategy games.
Pros: Great story, amazing gameplay, Awesome roleplaying turn based strategy game.
Cons: No map, No stealing or fight with anyone, Music is weak.

Disclaimer: This review is for people who have lots of time on their hands. It's probably going to be long.
As I always do,I'll divide this review into several smaler parts, starting with the Story.
By the way, spoilers are everywhere, but I'm still going to put a "Spoiler Arrow" at the begining of every "Spoiler Part". With that being said, here we go!
- Story
-----> Spoiler warning for the Story! Go to the next arrow to skip the spoiler!
There really isn't much of a story. You're a new kid, who just moved into town and who (probably) just wants to make friends. Your parents say that they moved for a reason and since we haven't played what happened before you move into town, they think you've forgotten it. As you go outside you meet your first companion, Buters. He takes you to the Kingdom of Kupa Keep, a fortress that has been built and is ruled by Cartman and the humans. Their Enemey are the (Drow)Elves, led by Kyle. You're at Kupa Keep when you suddenly get attacked by the Elves and you try to protect "The stick of Truth" wich essentially lets the one that has it rule the universe. At least that's what they're believing. They defeat the Elves but the Stick of Truth (now refered to SoT by me) was stolen. Cartman told Clyde to watch out for it, but he failed. Cartman banns Clyde from Space and Time (Or in other words, he kicks him out of their game). Your next objective is now to recruit new people to your group. You want the Goths to join you, and as you were about to do that you get intercepted by the elves. They take you to Kyle, who wants you to recriut the Goths for the Elves and not for the Humans. And now, it's your choice. Will you betray Cartman or will you... Ah ♥♥♥♥ it, let's just betray that fatass. You enter the school to fight Cartman and after all of that is done, you find out that Clyde has stolen the stick (he's just a bad looser). The only way to beat him is by recruiting more people, including the most dangerous of them all: GIRLS! Anyways, you infiltrate Clydes tower and battle to the top. At the top you meet Mr. Slave, who has a "snuke" in his♥♥♥♥♥♥ There is a Secret ending here. Just leave the room and you'll get it. Or you'll just shrink down is size and go into his♥♥♥♥♥
aft(h)er that, you finally fight Clyde... well, not really, you fight the Nazi Zombie Chef. But then, you're ready for the final fight! You find out that the reason you moved was , in fact, not you ability to fart like a pro but make tons of friend in a matter of seconds. The CIA's  leader takes the Stick, goes nuts and runs to the final fight. Kenny also switches to his side. Now you might ask you self: "Where does this mysterious goo come from and how can you shrink in size?" Thats pretty easy: On night 1, You encounter an alien ship and you get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥by an anal-probe.

Overall this is one of my favorite games (and series) of all time. I think they did a fantastic job of creating an original world and environment that is very easy to immerse yourself in. It's creepy, but it feels natural and never forced. I think that collecting the audio, video, and text logs that explain what has been happening on the Ishimura go a long way to creating the atmosphere. Other games of this type have suffered because of their collectables, but not this one.
However, I don't really think that it is a pure survival-horror game. It is definitely heavy on the action, but does not suffer from that at all. Rather I think it makes it more accesable for people who aren't really into horror games in the first place. I hate pure horror games and movies in general, but absolutely love this game (and the series as a whole). The scares don't come from not being able to deal with enemies or having to avoid them, but rather the atmosphere and environment coupled with the excellent creature design.
Definitely worth a pick up even if you aren't a fan of the genre.

I really recommend this title if you love Survival Horror games, really worths every penny you spend on it.

Alright, after about 102 hours of playing this game, let me write a review.
Boy was the development of this game a ♥♥♥♥ing trip. Within the first year of Early Access release, Tripwire failed to listen to the communities complaints and suggestions, the game was horrendously unbalanced, and holy♥♥♥♥♥♥was there no content. Not to mention they'd delete any negative criticism of their game from their forums.
BUT.
Tripwire seems to have gotten the memo, and now equipped with a full team again, seem to be making a much more polished game. I write this review after playing the new Beta patch that introduced the SWAT perk and various reworks of existing perks, as well, to my surprise, added additional weapons to pre-existing perks (Such as the Katana being added to berseker and the M16 added to Demo). After this patch I find myself not being able to get enough Killing Floor 2 in my blood stream. Maybe it's the excitement for my fancy new in game Canadian ball cap, or maybe it's that the game actually FEELS ENJOYABLE now. I used to compare Tripwire to the guys who made District 9: First they made a rugget, low budget movie that was really good, and people loved it (District 9), and they got so much money from that that they said they were going to make another great movie, which ended up flopping because in reality they have no idea what they're doing (Elysium). Obviously this analogy is no longer true, and I think if you played the game in its current state you'd agree. I feel, and I hope, that it's only going to get better from here.
Before I wrap up this review, let me hit you with a few final pros and cons.
PROS:
-Extremely fun, fast paced Co-Op gameplay
-Wide Variety of cosmetics, perks, and hopefully one day weapons
-Powerful weaponry, audio is fantastic
-Amazing, get you pumped soundtrack (Who doesn't love a  bit of Demon Hunter?)
-Great work shop modding community
CONS:
-Still fairly unbalanced
-Each perk has an average of 4 weapons
-Fairly slow to update
-No Chickenator
[EDIT: Demolitionist projectiles not exploding at close range is a feature.]

I find it hard to believe that a game released in 2004, can still surprise me 10 years later.
Extremely late to the show, this year marked the first time I ever touched the Half Life Franchise in my life, other than some casual games of Counter Strike at a friend's house. Still, there is a reason the second game in this franchise is considered by many to be one of the greatest games of all time, and after so long, I finally get the hype.
Graphics are slightly dated, but hold up to this day, especially with mods and all the HD texture packs, you'll find it has about the same level of visual fidelity as Portal 2, a game released in 2011 for god's sake! Story and audio are all passable, not exceptional, but above average.
What really does it for this game though, is of course the game play, which should be the most important aspect of any game. To start with, I find it really hard to like first person shooters, this is the only exception besides Portal which isn't really a shooter to begin with, but what this game does is incorporate tonnes of physics into the shooting, which makes for a whole tonne of fun.
To give you a sense of what I mean, I think I spent half the game using a crow bar and a gravity gun.

This isn't a review of the specific game but a warning that may not work if you are using a modern PC. The game's engine is connected with the game's framerate, thus framerate limiter needs to be on for the game to work properly. If you don't have the limiter on the game appears to run smoothly but your car will be moving slower, and you will not be able to back up in the car (this applies to all vehicles, this makes the boat missions impossible, and any racing mission is impossible). There are also varous glitches that happen during missions because the engine wasn't design to be played at a high framerate.
So why not play with the framerate limiter on? Well for me the game looks horribly choppy with it on, with noticable drops in frames continously.
The game may work better if you have an old processor or graphics card possibly? I would recommend just getting it on the PS2 where you know it will work and you will have better controls too!

Simply a fun zombie filled shooter with plenty of gore. A good amount of classes are playable as of this writing which each have their pros and cons. A good chunk of the maps are fun but it definitely needs more and some are quite a miss in terms of popularity. If your desire is to blast the brains out of wave after wave of zombies, this game fulfills those desires. I can't find any real negative things to point out beyond needing more maps, more bosses, and a gradual increase in class choices. The other component that I don't find so well done is the free loot drops. Unless you are planning to spend money to unlock them, they feel quite worthless and you will receive them pretty frequently. They are now on a 24 hour cooldown with a higher increase for skins which is nice but it would be nice to have the option to disable the boxes that require keys for those who most definitely will not be opening them.
There isn't much to say in terms of positive comments beyond what is mentioned as the first few sentences summarized the game. Pick a map, pick a class (changeable between waves), kill zombies and live while buying better guns. It is a simple enough concept and very enjoyable. The additions of players being able to be zombies vs survival players is a good addition for some variation, granted I have not tried this mode.
The devs are consistently working on adding to this game, granted it feels rather slow. Maps came out much faster for Killing Floor 1. At the moment we see a map or two every 3 to 4 months? Currently there are around 9 total so it can feel a bit repetitive when about 6 of those are good and the remainders missing the mark. As long as free updates continue, this game will continue to be something to incorporate to a regular lineup of games or relax with in the evenings, alone or with others.

Even for those who never played the SNES or Genesis games, or played the tabletop version, this game stands firmly on its own as a great game.  The main storyline is broken up into segments that are almost chapter-like, or perhaps could be thought of as "one night stands" if you're familiar with the vernacular, which makes finding places to take a break a comfortable matter.  It is expertly written, very enjoyable, and immersive.
The combat mechanics are tactical, and for the most part leave a little room for error in case you pull a significant gaffe (note: burst attacks harm both enemies and allies, so don't do that in big important boss battles).  My only complaint would be that the interface for combat can be a touch clunky, though for the most part it was pretty intuitive.  Any frustrations were brief, primarily user-error, and did not get in the way of exploring the mystery at hand.
Steam Workshop support means that this game provides a framework for further stories made by the community.  The only downfall?  No multiplayer.  Now that I've played it once, I would love to share an adventure with a friend or two!  Regardless, I would rate this game as highly recommended.

GTA Vice City - A true, timeless masterpiece, that has endured the test of time and is still one of the best games in the series.
Just like all older games, this one does not strike you with stunning visuals, like the newer additions in the series like GTA IV and V. But graphics is not all about a game. GTA Vice City offers a great story, characters and the feeling of freedom in its beautiful open-world city, that only few other games manage to capture.
The refferences to the pop culture of the 80s are to be found literaly everywhere in Vice City, which accomplishes the atmosphere of the 80s' Miami, which the game aims to recreate in its own unique style.  The style of the people that you see in the streets, the cars, the buildings' architecture and the scenery all help you immerse with the game and makes you feel as if you are watching a movie, rather than playing a game.
The soundtrack that Rockstar have compiled is divine, topping even those from the newer entries in the GTA series. All the radio stations in the game are absolutely fantastic with songs from the titans of the 80s' musical scene like Michael Jackson, Ozzy Osbourne, Mr. Mister, Toto, INXS, Laura Brannigan and many others. Even if you don't like this kind of music, the game will make you fall in love with it. But there's more - the radio stations' DJs will make you laugh all the time with their comments on topics that satirize different aspects of the life in the 80s. And the commercials too!
The story of the game is also brilliant. As if it is directly taken from a classical gangster movie. Filled with action, twists and many great characters you will be thrilled from the start and until the very end. But even after the completion of all the story missions you will have to spend many more hours if you want to unlock 100% of the game. The game will offer you more than at least 20 hours of sheer fun, but no doubt you will want to come back again and play it over and over again. But if you don't like playing by the rules, you will still be able to find lots of fun things to do. Steal a car, go on a rampage, attain a six-star wamted level and have some fun blowing up police and military vehicles and shooting SWAT teams with tons of great weapons, as they try to stop you.
More than 10 years after its initial release GTA Vice City is still the excellent game it used to be. If you have not had the chance to play the game until now, do not hesitate and get it right away.

Simply a fun zombie filled shooter with plenty of gore. A good amount of classes are playable as of this writing which each have their pros and cons. A good chunk of the maps are fun but it definitely needs more and some are quite a miss in terms of popularity. If your desire is to blast the brains out of wave after wave of zombies, this game fulfills those desires. I can't find any real negative things to point out beyond needing more maps, more bosses, and a gradual increase in class choices. The other component that I don't find so well done is the free loot drops. Unless you are planning to spend money to unlock them, they feel quite worthless and you will receive them pretty frequently. They are now on a 24 hour cooldown with a higher increase for skins which is nice but it would be nice to have the option to disable the boxes that require keys for those who most definitely will not be opening them.
There isn't much to say in terms of positive comments beyond what is mentioned as the first few sentences summarized the game. Pick a map, pick a class (changeable between waves), kill zombies and live while buying better guns. It is a simple enough concept and very enjoyable. The additions of players being able to be zombies vs survival players is a good addition for some variation, granted I have not tried this mode.
The devs are consistently working on adding to this game, granted it feels rather slow. Maps came out much faster for Killing Floor 1. At the moment we see a map or two every 3 to 4 months? Currently there are around 9 total so it can feel a bit repetitive when about 6 of those are good and the remainders missing the mark. As long as free updates continue, this game will continue to be something to incorporate to a regular lineup of games or relax with in the evenings, alone or with others.
Personal experience score: 9.5/10
Story: -/10 - N/A, you shoot zombies in a wave style match
Sound: 10/10 - Lots of epic music. This really adds to the experience of just sitting down to listen to some quality metal music while blasting the brains out of zombies
Graphics: 9/10 - Great but not realistic, just keep that in mind. The FLEX component needs some optimization and it can stutter on occassion.
Controls: 10/10 - Nothing wrong here
Game Length: 10/10 - Infinite playability. It will take about 300 hours to level all the classes as of this writing on hard difficulty.

Some downsides:
* The save-point system. Ouch. Sometimes you just have real-world things happening that mean you want to save and exit. You just can't do that with this game. One crash, one bad move or one girlfriend that needs attention and you'll be looking at doing that last hour over again.
* I'm sure there probably is a manual, but I haven't found it yet. This means that when you're playing the game, you have to just randomly assign points as nothing is explained well.
* The inventory system. There isn't one really, its just that bad.
Overall 7/10

Obviously Arkham Knight hasn't had the best introduction to Steam and thus it has left a bad taste in many peoples mouths. Fortunately it has been fixed and in my experience it is very much playable. However it's far from the epic conclusion we might have expected.
Arkham Knight, of course, follows from Arkham City and is a very personal story for Batman which actually hinders the game. It seems as though several ideas were mashed together and I don't think it works very well. It's satsifying at times but you question the choices made by Rocksteady.
It plays like the previous Arkham games in regards to combat in conjunction with detective mode being heavily overused to complete your objective/track hostiles. You actually get mocked by someone for using it and I like to think that's an inside joke.
Also The Riddler is back and he's even more annoying than before!
The biggest new feature is the Batmobile and that is both a strength and a weakness. It's great fun utilising it to feel more like Batman but it's also a tank to blow certain 'things' up, not to mention use non-lethal rounds on hostiles. You can eject from it and glide around central Gotham but it's not necessary because you can use the grapnel boost much more effectively; thereby eliminating the need for it as a travel option. Not to mention gliding is so much more fun.
New gadgets appear and make Batman look like he's camping as you hide on your gargoyle/perch. Though fear takedown is a lot of fun.
Teaming up with various partners, main game, is great because you have exceptional banter between Batman + whomever and you can switch between the two partners.
DLC for the game, so far, is horribly short but still fun to control distinctive characters (except Azrael). This is a highlight for me as the playable characters in AR missions/DLC are so different when it comes to fighting styles. This actually encourages me to want to play the AR missions.
This will appeal to fans of the previous games because of multiple reasons; my own being it is a continuation of the series and I love Batman.
It's a very tough one because I love the series a great deal but the main story is not satisfying at all. At times it feels like it's been padded out with Batmobile sections when it could focus elsewhere. Some missions feel too short whilst others involve new (to Arkham) characters that are more fun- Professor Pyg and Manbat being two of those.
I'll recommend this because I still enjoyed it and believe that it's worth playing because it gets Batman so right. Often you feel like a detective and not just a stalker of meglomaniacs. Combat is approachable for different playstyles and it has plenty of side missions for you to take a breather.
But by the Gods I damn well HATE the Riddler.

This game is truly phenominal.  Sucked into a world where up is down, left is right, floors and walls disappear before your eyes only to find out you're back where you started. Every aspect of this game is built to mess with your mind, and the puzzles are the most solid and interesting i've seen in any game to date.The puzzles themselves aren't in a linear "complete one, do the next one" structure. Every corner you turn has another brain teaser waiting behind it, and the order you encounter puzzles is only determined by your curiosity to explore the world. The game world and soundtrack work incredibly well together to make you feel constantly uncomfortable with your surroundings. But the greatest feeling you get from the game is the sense of achievement when you conquer one of the many unconventional puzzles, which allows you to progress forward and stumble upon a sign theat tells you to turn around and you realise the area you just walked through is no longer there, thus reapplying that curiosity that's driven you throughout the entire game. Yes this truly is a masterpiece.

If you like roguelikes and don't mind very basic visuals (kind of goes hand-in-hand with liking roguelikes...), this is the game for you.   Requiring equal parts luck and skill (and believe me, you'll need both) and an enthusiasm for micromanagement, FTL is a brutally unforgiving journey through the stars that almost always ends in the unfortunate destruction of your ship or crew - frequently both. There's enough depth to the gameplay and unlockables to acquire to keep the experience fresh for hundreds of playthroughs, each of which can take anywhere from 10 minutes to 4 or 5 hours, depending on your performance (or lack thereof).  Each moment in FTL offers a new chance for complete annihilation of everything you've worked so hard for, and you'll be cursing out loud at your monitor in no time, but this is also why you'll love it.  Essentially what I'm saying is this: FTL is the best abusive relationship 10 bucks can buy.

A really fun turn based strategy/rpg game, that unfortunately is a bit short on its own without mods.
Basically to compare this game to a more recent game, i would compare it to x-com: enemy unknown.  The big difference is that cover is not as important, and Shadowrun has a lot more rpg elements.  There are several classes/races to start as (anything from mages to hackers and humans to giant mutant trolls) you can mix and match classes as you see fit (so mage samurai hacker is certainly feasible).
As far as art style i'd compare it to things like the matrix deus ex. and ghost in the shell.  If  those things catch your fancy then this is right up your alley.  (I guess shadowrun is something that's been around for a LONG time but its never been something i've been aware of.)
The only drawback is the length of the game.  It can easily be completed in around 10 hours and that just doesn't seem like a long enough game to fool around with a lot of the great RPG elements they have.  The length of the game sort of punishes you for trying to make a hybrid character and forces you to develop your character along a certain path to be strong enough for the end game (I.E. No real optional missions to build up xp and money).  This isn't too much of a problem as it may have been at release though because there are several mods out now that add loads of additional content and tweaks that will give you plenty of incentive to keep going with your first character or make whole new ones.
The story is pretty decent, but if you don't like reading a lot of text you may be in for a disappointment.  You have to be paitent and read a lot of the dialogue to catch subtle hints on how to solve problems and get clues.  I think my biggest gripe with the story once again has to do with the length of the game however.  You meet a lot of really interesting characters, but it just seems like their stories drop off when they begin to get interesting, making you think "wait is that it?"  The game is set up big time for sequels/spin-offs and i'm not sure if the devs just made a short campaign and gave it to the community to develop everything or if sometime down the road they will be releasing additional campaigns of their own.
Overall a really great rpg/strategy/turn based combat game, which is just too short; but fear not mods abound that will make the game enjoyable and replayable for a long time to come.

The Stick of Truth has you playing as the new kid in South Park, meeting the gang, and going on one hell of an adventure full of might, magic, and literal piles of♥♥♥♥♥♥
This game is fantastic if you are already a South Park fan. It's full of references and in-jokes that you can't help but give an obnoxious "Ha!" when they show up. All the references and hidden gags make exploring things a lot more entertaining than I would have originally expected from the game.
Of course, the voice acting and art style are fantastic and stay 100% true to the source material (big surprise). It feels like an interactive episode of South Park, which I didn't know I wanted until I played this game.
Another nice thing I really appreciated is that the game isn't abnormaly long. I was able to finish the main storyline and some of the side quests in about 17 hours without rushing. I feel like if this game were to have had a much longer campaign or have been padded out with mandatory side quests to finish the game, it would have just dragged on too long. It's like being asked to watch a 30+ hour long South Park episode; some people might like it, and sure it would probably be pretty good for the first half of it or so, but I feel like it would just get stale.
The combat is also pretty enjoyable. I was worried since the idea of turn-based combat typically puts me to sleep. However, South Park keeps it entertaining with at least requiring some form of interaction from the player. Not to mention I was surprised at how I actually needed to think through my strategies to beat certain opponents as opposed to the combat being so simple that it would merely be an obstacle between cutscenes.
There are some downsides, of course. One being that while there are side quests in the game and going through them can be fun for the purpose of experiencing more inside jokes and references, they are all pretty basic fetch and collecting quests that get very repetitive. The main storyline stays pretty entertaining though with a decently wide variety of missions to play that aren't all copy-paste of the same style.
Other than that and some minor glitches I encountered in my playthrough, I genuinely enjoyed this game. It had a lot more depth in the gameplay mechanics than I had originally expected and on top of that it's just a damn funny game for South Park fans. I'd highly recommend if you're a fan of the show, even if you're not typically a fan of RPGs or turn-based combat systems.

There are a couple of mini games (if you can call them that) that can get a little frustrating at times, but that is the only downside I found through my play through.

The bottom line is that Shadowrun Returns is a truly wonderful experience from beginning to end and reminds me why I fell in love with both the video game and tabletop versions of the Sixth World in the early 90s and how it’s influenced me ever since (I was a Cyberdog shill for a while people. I practically dressed like some of the characters in this game!) The entire experience is top notch and I just hope we don’t have to go another twenty years before we get another high quality video game version of Shadowrun. Hell, the engine is solid enough that I could even see Harebrained doing short episodic Shadowrun games, a la the current tabletop Shadowrun Missions lines. If you own this already, you already know why I love this. If you don’t own it yet, then my god man or woman, what are you waiting for? It’s only $19.99 for the basic version on Steam. Just go get it already. Otherwise you’re missing out on not just one of the best PC games of 2013 or one of the best RPGs of 2013, but one of the best games across the board for this year and why would you want to deprive yourself of that?

There's a lot of decision making in this game and the rest is left to some chance. If you've ever wanted to feel like Captain Picard of the USS Enterprise, download this game.

Do not buy this game if you want a good story. Do not buy this game if you're into awesome graphics. Do not buy this game if you can't deal with a little permadeath. Do not buy this game if you want a game that hands you all the unlockables and characters on a silver platter. Do not buy this game... Well, you get the idea.
On the other hand, if you fit none of the above categories, you're golden. Risk of Rain is a Sci-Fi Roguelike which makes no excuses and no apologies. The story is minimal, the environments are decent if simple, and the gameplay is very, very unforgiving. And yes, you WILL die on your first run, I guarantee you. But soldier on, young gamer. Early runs are mostly dedicated to unlocking new characers (of which there are 12) and getting used to the game's mechanics. As the singular survivor (or survivors, if playing multiplayer) of a space shuttle crash, you must navigate a hostile alien planet in an effort to return to your spaceship, which has been commandeered by a mysterious alien named Providence. Beyond that, there's very little storytelling to be seen. Just survive to the end, gathering items and slaughtering your foes as you level up your character and try to make sense of what exactly is happening around you. As your character leaves the planet at the end of the final level, the camera pans over the level you've just finished, showing the piles of corpses of seemingly innocent creatures you just carved your way through to make it off the planet. You've survived- but at what cost?
Bittersweet ending aside, the game is a wild ride. Every one of the 12 characters is unique to play and powerful when mastered, from the agile and well-rounded Commando to the DOT-heavy, hit-and-run Acrid, to the bulky, slow-moving HAN-D. Enemies and bosses are varied, and each is unique in approach and danger level. While blasting your way through the armies of aliens is a fun time, don't take too long- the difficulty ramps up steadlily the longer your session goes on, and if you dawdle long enough, the RNG will happily toss legions of bosses and powered-up Elite enemies in place of the lowly mooks you've been fighting up to that point. Balancing steady progression and staying around long enough to grab all the helpful items and buffs is a constant struggle, even while you're trying to avoid getting torn to shreds by hostile wildlife.
I've greatly enjoyed all of the time I've spent with Risk of Rain. And if you're willing to soldier on through death and brutal death, I'm sure you will too.

Civ 5 is an all around good game. It's certainly best to play it with friends, so put this into consideration when buying it. Unless you're desperate to get the game, I would also recommend waiting until a Steam Sale, because I managed to get all of the game's content for 8 pounds, which, considering it would usually cost around 100 pounds, I would say is a bargain. The Civilisation series is more focused around the diplomacy and politics of running a vast empire, and is less centered around combat. Therefore, if you are looking for an RTS (Real Time Strategy) game that is centered around combat, I would recommend looking at the Total War series. The random map generation and vast array of units in the game makes it very diverse and fun! Civ 5 is a good game to play with friends, however, they will soon become your enemies.
I do believe I will never pay a single penny for another Tripwire product.

The game world and soundtrack work incredibly well together to make you feel constantly uncomfortable with your surroundings. Yes this truly is a masterpiece.

"She canna take it no more, capt'n!", you hear your brave fellow officer calling from the burning engine room as the enemy lasers pound your hull. The fire keeps spreading to the next room and the alarms scream as you rush from the shield centre to help him weld that critical hull crack, even though you know the shields are giving way any second. Your weapons officer gets overrun by incoming mantises teleporting into your ship just as he launches a missile that misses the enemy ship by an inch. But alas, it's too late and your ship exploses into a million little pieces.
Part Space Alert, part Red November and infused with some EGA Trek, "FTL: Faster Than Light" is just an awesome little indie game, originally concieved via Kickstarted. Simplicity is key when creating these Star Trekish spacefaring scenarios, where the only thing standing between chaos and disasterous events that threten to destroy your little spacevessel is you and your brave crew. As a filler game, FTL is pure fun!

Dead Space is an action oriented survival horror game.
You are Isaac Clarke, an engineer that is part of a rescue team. Your mission is to repair the spaceship USG Ishimura, a huge mining vessel that carves out chunks from planets and harvests the valuable ore. Shortly after they arrive on board all hell breaks loose. Their craft is destroyed, leaving them stranded on the Ishimura. The crew is attacked by nightmarish creatures. Seperated from the others it is up to Isaac to wander the halls, search for any friends or survivors that are still alive and fix as many problems as he can until he can find a way to escape the ship.
The setting is where the game shines. It definitely feels like you are in deep space. There are sections in a vacuum, things sound differently as you would expect if you were in an airless environment. You also have a small air supply that will run out if you are not quickly. There are other parts where there is no gravity and you can leap from floor to ceiling or walk up the sides of a wall.
A cool aspect is that there is no HUD. Health is displayed on the back of your suit and ammunition is displayed when you hold up your weapon.
Another interesting feature is the holographic screens that appear throughout the ship and when someone is talking to you. All elevators and doors have one of these screens instead of a standard switch.
The graphics are good. It has great lighting effects, textures, and models.
The sounds also really help with the immersion. You will sometimes hear random clanking, footsteps, or alien grunts and shrieks that keep you on your toes. The music gets intense when you are under attack by a group of aliens and is kind of spacey when you are just exploring alone.
Overall, if you like blood, gore, horror and action you should try Dead Space. There might be too much action in this game for the old school survival-horror fans but it should still be ok for them.

Questo FTL - Faster Than Light (grazie al cielo che il titolo è in inglese, il corrispettivo termine italiano è Velocità Superluminare, e nessuno vuole giocare a qualcosa con un nome così brutto), rinchiude tutto ciò che un RogueLike dovrebbe avere, con la differenza che al posto del nostro classico eroe solitario questa volta dovremo portare la nostra astronave alla fine dell'universo! La storia è semplicissima, ma tanto non serve a nessuno conoscerla: abbiamo rubato dei preziosissimi piani segreti e dobbiamo portarli in salvo alla fine dell'universo, mentre tutta la flotta galattica di non ricordo quale fazione ci starà alle calcagna, avanzando a rastrelliera, galassia dopo galassia, per trovarci e sterminarci. L'universo, in questo gioco, è rappresentato come una fila di galassie da esplorare (otto, per la precisione), ognuna composta da un buon numero di "punti di interesse" tra cui possiamo trovare richieste di aiuto, campi di asteroidi, pianeti in guerra, navi pirata pronti a tenderci una trappola e utilissimi negozi spaziali (oltre a tanti eventi più o meno unici, a cui possiamo reagire in diversi modi a seconda del nostro equipaggiamento e della composizione della nostra ciurma). Oltre all'ansia di aver alle spalle tutta l'armata galattica, dovremo fare i conti anche con il nostro serbatoio di carburante: ad ogni salto interstellare (ovvero un movimento da un punto della mappa ad un altro) consumeremo una unità di preziosa benzina, costringendoci a pianificare un poco i movimenti e spesso mandandoci alla ricerca  di negozi in cui fare rifornimento (o ad assaltare una nave civile rubandogli qualsiasi cosa).

GTA: Vice City was one of my all-time favorite games when I was younger, and I'm not ashamed to admit that a big reason for that was because you could just do all sorts of horrible things and get away with it over and over again. Coming back and playing it now, I can really appreciate just how much effort was put into making this game as over-the-top ridiculous and silly as possible. As of writing this, I've played this game for 35 hours, and I still haven't quite finished the major storyline. Although probably less than half of that time was spent actually doing missions or propelling the story and instead just me racing or beating up random people or blowing up boats and helicopters with a machine gun, I feel that every minute of play was worth it, and I definitely think it's worth the entire $10, especially since it's usually half-off during every sale that ever happens.
For those people who might disregard this game out of hand because it's just another criminal power fantasy game with no substance... well, you're only partially right. Vice City puts you in the shoes of Tommy Vercetti, a low-level criminal with a sharp mind and a pension for violence, and you slowly work your way up to pretty much running the entire city's underground. During your trip, you'll come across crude and tasteless jokes that really only appeal to the immature child in you, but if you pay attention, you will find that nearly all of the jokes in the game are satirical and either make fun of the ridiculousness of some cliche stereotypes (Congressman Shrub, Love Fist, and Ken Rosenberg come to mind), or they wildly exaggerate something just to show how stupid it is. These can range from the obvious (The Degenetron, Giggle Cream, Banco Corrupto Grande, and Salivex), to slightly more subtle ones (The names of a few missions are the easiest examples).
My absolute favorite part of this game is just how much there is to do, there's like 50 different kinds of cars, 5-10 trucks, 5-ish vans, 5-ish helicopters, 3 RC vehicles, 3 different cop cars, a firetruck, an ambulance, two taxis, 4 bikes, 2 scooters, a dune buggy, a plane, a tank, a swat truck, 3 military vehicles, a luggage cart, a golf cart, and like 15 boats that you can drive, pilot, ride, or otherwise make go. There are 100 hidden packages to collect, every 10 of which unlocks a weapon or body armor at up to three of the about 20 properties you can own. You can deliver "ice cream", take the injured to a hospital, drive fares around the city, do some vigilante work, put out some fires, then go to the mall and order a burger or stop at a pizza place, and pick up a slice before you start delivering some yourself. There are rampage tokens that challenge you to just go on a mass-murdering spree for 2 minutes, There are copious random weapons lying all over town you can pick up to expand your arsenal, then you can head over to the ammunation in downtown and practice at the shooting range. After all of that, there are side missions you can complete for one of the assets you buy around Vice City, or you can carry out a contract for Mr. Black, who only contacts you by phone. And if you just feel like doing nothing, while you're in/on a vehicle, you can listen to one of several radio stations, each with a full day (in-game) of content that just goes beyond absurd (Thor speaks on kchat, Pastor Richards talks about his cult on VCPR, and Fernando Martinez reveals his secrets for masculinity and power on Emotion 98.3). Oh yeah, there are also a few easter-eggs for those of you willing to look.
Seriously, I cannot recommend this game enough. If you have the cash to spare, please consider picking this up; I can almost garuntee you won't regret it.

TL;DR - 9/10, RockSteady fixed the issues that plagued the PC release, another great Batman game! If you liked Arkham Asylum and Arkham City, GET IT!
WARNING - MINOR SPOILERS AHEAD!!!
=-=-=-=-=-=-=
This is very much like Arkham City in design, but RockSteady has added a few wonderful things to the mix which keep it fresh and new. The new suit lets you get around the city more quickly and the new Fear takedowns are fun, but the real beauty in this game lies in the addition of...wait for it...
... the BatMobile.
*Disclamer: I am HORRIBLE at driving games. Utterly awful. Can't do it. Never could.
If there is one area where this game ***could** have fallen apart, the BatMobile and driving around the city is it. The open world game Mad Max had time trial missions that were almost impossible to complete and that robbed me of some of the enjoyment of the game. However, RockSteady has avoided every possible pitfall that I could think of with driving around in Gotham and has made the addition of the BatMobile another exercise in fun. If *I* can finish the driving challenges in this game, ANYONE can. The car-to-tank mechanic allows for easy maneuvering around tight turns and narrow areas, and the coolness factor of the car and the tank cannot be overemphasized.
Now for the negative: I did have to go to the controller for the driving time trials, as well as one of the side missions during the game. If, like me, you are a completionist when it comes to open-world games, you'll probably need a controller to get through everything.
Am I nitpicking? Pretty sure I'm nitpicking. Yeah, I think I'm nitpicking.
I've played through about 15% of the main storyline and some of the side missions, and I'm hooked. Great Riddler puzzles, lots of combat combos, all the good stuff you've come to expect from RockSteady's Batman games.

Bottom line: this in an INCREDIBLE game with a DULL ENDING.
What happened with the PC version of this game is almost tragic. It's been infamous because of its terrible port to PC, but if you are able to run it and play it, you'll discover probably one of the best AAA games ever made.
If you like Batman as a characters of have enjoyed the previous Arkham games, you'll probably love this one as well. Its story is spectacular, to say the least, with several memorable moments and conversations between Batman and his close associates.
I played the game on a PC with a Gigabyte GTX 770 4GB GPU, an I7 3770 CPU and a Sandisk SSD. When I capped the game FPS at 60 or 90, I experienced wide variations in performance, like many users, and it was very noticeable during the game. However, when I capped FPS at 30, the game never fell under 29 fps and performed steadily with that framerate. I know that for many players, that's unacceptable, but since I played the other Arkham titles on my PS3 at 30 fps, I could play this one with that framerate without any trouble.
That said, there are two aspects of the game that I didn't like that much: the Riddler challenges and the ending.
Somewhere I read that this game had a "good" ending and a "bad" ending, and that in order to get the "good" ending you had to arrest all the main enemies, including the Riddler. And to be able to fight and capture the Riddler, you have to finish all the Riddler challenges.
I love side missions and I even loved the Riddlers challenges which were part of the game story. But in order to complete all the additional Riddler challenges, I had to literally spend days tracking and solving them -many of them were pretty clever- but it totally drove me away from the main story during that period. I would have put all those additional Riddler challenges in a DLC or something. There's also not a "good" or "bad"ending; apparently, they are the same, one is just "complete" and the other one "incomplete".
Many players probably liked the ending, just like many people liked the Batman movies' ending. I didn't like either. I don't like open endings. But that's just a matter of opinion.
Many players have complained about the overuse of the Batmobile. I actually enjoyed many sections with the car, but I agree it was probably too much. There are parts when you HAVE to use the Batmobile to advance in the main story. I would have probably given a choice, as a developer, to use the car or find another solution with Batman for the people that didn't like to use the Batmobile that much.
I know that the car is a very big thing in American culture, but it always made more sense to me that Batman -as a character based on a flying creature- should resort more to the Batwing. Sadly, that flying marvel is used in the game just as a delivery and multipurpose drone.
So, to wrap this up, if you liked the previous Arkham games and you manage to run this one, you'll very probably love it!

If this game is ever under $10, jump on it. It is definitely worth it for that price, but I bought it on the Summer Sale, with all the DLC for about $18, and I feel a little salty about it. I'm a huge fan of the Arkham series, so my review is mostly comparing Arkham Knight to the others. Look, this is, in every aspect, another Arkham game. That said, it has a base level of quality. It looks pretty good even with the graphics set to low across the board. But compared to the rest of the series, it is far away the worst of the bunch.
The batmobile was a nice thought, but the controls are terrible. You feel like you're driving on ice the whole game, and I'm sorry, but with the big♥♥♥♥♥tread on those tires, Brucie isn't sliding anywhere unless he wants to. And even with the addition, I STILL had more fun zipping and gliding around Gotham. There are some interesting things to see from the Batmobile, but roof/air travel is still the only efficient means of getting around the city quickly.
My biggest issue with this Arkham entry was the combat. The Arkham Series' minimal button combat, which rewards timing over mashing, is among my favorites in action games. But the combat just seems. . .  off in this one. The timing is so picky compared to City and Origins, which caused me to fight around the edges of a mob rather than jumping right into the middle of the fray (as I believe Batman would in similar scenarios). As a result, it signifcantly limited the way I could fight, navigate within the group, and even the moves I could use. In larger fights I found myself reverting to the basic "pinball" fight mechanics, because all the fancy moves and gadget techs I had acquired were more dangerous than efffective.
An mechanic addition I REALLY liked was the Fear Multi-Takedown. This is an incredibly useful tool in predator situations, and I think it's a super fun way to start off a fight. Your FEAR guage is refilled by silently taking out enemies, or over time. If you have full fear, and you can sneak close enough to a group of enemies, you can initiate the Multi-takedown, highlighting enemies and beating them down one by one in a bullet-time style interactive custcene. It's intensely gratifying. Trust me. However, I have a feeling the developer didn't intend it to be used for combat as extensively as I did. It's not a big deal, I guess, I just would have liked more flexibility with how I exercized the option.
As for the story, (**NO SPOILERS HERE**) this is obviously the last game in the Arkham Trilogy (whatever that means). Fans of the series knew it before the release, and the plot makes it painfully, hurtfully clear about a gillion more times. But, even with that in mind, the ending is flat out dumb. It's anti-climactic, and it was a very serious let down for me personally. Until then, the story was a pretty standard Arkham affair. Just another night in Rocksteady's version of Gotham, which is to say: good, not great. But that ending. . . awful. There is a secret/additional ending if you 100% the game, which means finishing the side quests and collecting all those damn Riddler trophies. I am including that ending in my assessement of its stupidity.
Full disclosure: I bought the game and all the DLCs at once, so I can't really distinguish them all. But, there is some DLC that added a few more side quests to the vanilla game. These lead to some additional famous faces from Batman's extensive rougues gallery popping up in the main campaign. They essentially add an additional Most Wanted list to the base game. These DLCs, I loved. Anything that can make the story longer and more compelling, I'm on board.
The DLC AR missions, which are the stand alone combat and predator scenarios, are lame. Only because they focus so heavily on combat, which I was frustrated with from the get go. If you end up liking the short timing windows and extended counter animations, you'll love the extra AR missions, and more power to you.
Then there are the Arkham episodes. These are "story" driven mini adventures featuring some of Batman'sa supporting players (Nightwing, Robin, Catwoman, etc). They're. . . just. . .  dumb. Each one is basically just an excuse to take away certain fight moves and gadget abilities. (Which vanilla combat already does anyway.) For instance, every character in the game has a Scorpion-style grappling move that allows you to traverse the battlefield quickly, deal damage, and maintain your combo score. Oh, but Catwoman doesn't. SHE HAS A FREAKIN WHIP! Dumb.
I'm a huge Batman fan. A huge Arkham series fan. I was disappointed by this game, and I didn't even have to deal with any of the mess when it launched. (or when it re-launched and still sucked apparently.) Even if you feel an undeniable compulsion to play this game. PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE excerize patience. One day it will be $9.99. Then, and only then, will it be time to play Batman: Arkham Knight.

A really solid strategy adventure game. Similar to the old version from the SNES, or games like Fallout and Fallout Tactics. They even took some tips from the recently relaunched XCom title which is a little refreshing.
The game is played in two modes. Exploration mode and combat mode. Both take place in the same environment.
During exploration mode the player is free to walk around and inspect the area.
Once enemies show up things like shops and NPC's go away and the player takes out their weapon. The player now has limited actions per turn to fight the enemy. After defeating the enemies the player re-holsters their weapon and enters exploration mode.
The packaged campaign is fun and its multiple choices allow for replayability. The developers also relesed their devkit so players can make their own campaigns.

I want more games like this, and definitely more in the Shadowrun universe.
Shadowrun. Do you know Shadowrun? ... I'm not a nerdified loremaster, and certainly not qualified to make absolute statements, but from what I know Shadowrun is one of the largest RPG-Fiction-Universes ever created. It started out as  a Pen & Paper roll playing game with a nice, not overly-complicated mechanic and, which is the important thing, a really really cool setting. The whole Shadowrun universe is awesomely extensive, there exist around 50 or such novels about it aswell. To put it short: it's kind of a combination of William Gibson's Cyberpunk (Neuromancer, Biochips, Cyberspace, Mona Lisa Overdrive ...) and J.R.R. Tolkien's fantasy fiction (The Hobbit, Lord of the Rings). So, it's some moderate Sci-Fi (no laser guns or energy shields) intermingled with magic fantasy (Elves, Dwarves, Orcs... and pretty much every other creature you can think of).
Now, about the game... It's a turn based tactical combat game. The gameplay system is easy to grasp and usually doesn't eat as much time as other games with a similar gameplay concept sometimes do (the new X-Com for example). Graphics aren't breath-taking but entirely sufficient since most of the game really happens in the text based storytelling and interaction. Which get's me to the interesting part, the game's main story is really quite awesome, it's really been a while since I've seen a story as awesome as this one. The writing is entirely perfect, extremely immersive and complex, everything fits your characters race and gender, which in many other games is sadly neglected, and I've found like two typos in the whole game.
The game's atmosphere is rather dark, slums, gang-criminality, ruthless megacorporations and political apathy give a perfect backdrop for the story.
The game features an editor for custom campaign creation (there's a steam Workshop for it), which adds theoretically infinite replayability to it. Options for importing characters from campaign to campaign enable players to create characters with all-maxed out stats, if they so desire.
Options for equipment progression are quite limited -> 'at-the-moment' <-. A pretty extensive add-on for the game (Shadowrun-Returns: Dragonfall) has been announced and is due to be released in early 2014.
There is also an MMO Shadowrun game (Shadowrun-Online) in the tube, which I would recommend to check out aswell.
(PS: If anyone is interested in reading any of the above mentioned novels by William Gibson and/or J.R.R. Tolkien I explicitly recommend getting original english language prints, as the translations I've read for books of both authors really missed out on a lot of things.)

This is very much like Arkham City in design, but RockSteady has added a few wonderful things to the mix which keep it fresh and new. The new suit lets you get around the city more quickly and the new Fear takedowns are fun, but the real beauty in this game lies in the addition of...wait for it...
... the BatMobile.
*Disclamer: I am HORRIBLE at driving games. Utterly awful. Can't do it. Never could.
If there is one area where this game ***could** have fallen apart, the BatMobile and driving around the city is it. The open world game Mad Max had time trial missions that were almost impossible to complete and that robbed me of some of the enjoyment of the game. However, RockSteady has avoided every possible pitfall that I could think of with driving around in Gotham and has made the addition of the BatMobile another exercise in fun. If *I* can finish the driving challenges in this game, ANYONE can. The car-to-tank mechanic allows for easy maneuvering around tight turns and narrow areas, and the coolness factor of the car and the tank cannot be overemphasized.
Now for the negative: I did have to go to the controller for the driving time trials, as well as one of the side missions during the game. If, like me, you are a completionist when it comes to open-world games, you'll probably need a controller to get through everything.
Am I nitpicking? Pretty sure I'm nitpicking. Yeah, I think I'm nitpicking.
I've played through about 15% of the main storyline and some of the side missions, and I'm hooked. Great Riddler puzzles, lots of combat combos, all the good stuff you've come to expect from RockSteady's Batman games.

Risk of Rain is a platformer/sidescroller/survival game that puts you in control of one of a few survivors of a crashed spaceship. You will have to fight enemies and earn money to purchase upgrades and progress to the upper levels. The game's difficulty scales with the time, adding an incentive for players to use their time efficiently. In each individual "run" - or single playthrough - there are six levels, each with harder monsters and more expensive upgrades. Boss monsters appear at the end of a level or sometimes in the middle of a level if the difficulty is high enough. Risk of Rain will require several playthroughs to fully explore what all of the upgrades do and how to play each of the survivors.
Read more for an in-depth look at Risk of Rain.
This game's story is largely told in the beginning and end cutscenes, as well as in monster logs - information about enemies that randomly drop when you defeat one. Some of the descriptions in the item log also hint to background story events.
Risk of Rain [ROR] is a 2D pixelated platformer game. The art is excellent and each of the characters and enemies are unique. Each of the survivors has 4 unique abilities that are fairly balanced. Each one has their own forte and shortcomings, so experiment a little with all of them to figure out which one suits you. You only start with one character unlocked (the Commando), so you'll have to unlock the rest.
Items/upgrades are found in chests which unlock for a price. Monsters drop money and experience when killed, and both can also be found in small amounts within canisters. There are four ranks of upgrades - white (common), green (uncommon), red (rare) and orange (use item). The first three ranks are items that are either passive or triggered by events, while the fourth are items activated by the player. All use items and skills (except for the primary basic skill) have cooldowns. There is also an artifact hidden within each level. Artifacts do nothing in the run they are acquired in, but after that playthrough a new artifact's effect can be chosen in the character selection screen. Each one adds a different game element (only elites spawn, 500% damage but 10% health, etc).
ROR also has an incredible soundtrack, merging genres from electronic to trance to ambient to rock. Each level has its own exclusive background music, giving it a unique atmosphere. The sound effects are very believable and yet are alien enough to convince you that the planet you are on cannot be Earth.
Risk of Rain is an incredible platformer with solid gameplay mechanics, excellent replay value and an addicting arcade-style structure. Online multiplayer is also available. A solid game all-around. Definitely worth purchasing if you enjoy a good thrill.

Better than Binding of Isaac.  Yes, you heard me.
After consideration and playing for awhile now, I feel that Risk of Rain is a better rogue-like game than Binding of Isaac, perhaps even Rebirth.  Yes, you read right.
The reason why I feel this way is that BOI:Rebirth punishes players for using things like generated seeds by locking out achievements or forcing players to rely on random dumb luck to unlock things.  Risk of Rain on the other hand rewards players who ferret out the special artifacts that alter game play and do not penalize players for using them when it comes to unlocks.
Some people will feel that unlocks should not be the point of the game, but even without unlocks taken into consideration the artifacts allow players to really customize the feel -- from making things even harder than hard through using specific artifacts, to eliminating some of the randomization of drops so surviving as specific characters is less reliant on getting a good item early.  It makes the game feel less restricted in play.
At the heart of the game, there's still a tremendous amount of strategy involved in using the items you find to the best of your ability and class, with each class having drastically different play styles.  On top of it all, those who like the ludicrous over-powering of BOI:Rebirth should be satsified as it's quite possible to create that same feel using a combination of the right artifacts and items (and those who don't -- well you're covered as well).

A very light RPG mixed with a a very light tactical game.
The RPG part is very straightforward, it is not a HUB-spoke world.  You essentially play "levels" in the NES sense of the word.  There are conversations and dialog choices, but they are very straightforward and no wrong answers.  There is no going back to previous levels to do side quests.
The Tactical combat part is like a toned down X-COM.  Your characters have a percent chance to hit, you use light/medium/heavy cover to increase survivability and you have an overwatch ability to set up traps.
Your character can specialize in gun combat, melee combat, monk style chi, mage spellcasting, shaman spell casting/summoning, robot usage, and internet hacking (decking).
I went for street samuari and just improved my guns to be very powerful.  The nature of "shadowrunning" is hiring mercenaries to complete missions, so for every mission you choose a team of 3 people to help you out of maybe 30 choices.  What this means is that you can try out all the different classes without having to start a new game or hope that your hero is compatible with any "story heroes" (like in Baldurs gate, it was silly to choose a fighter/druid, when the first person who joins you is a fighter/druid).
You can also skip the class selection and just build your character however you want, so a submachine gun user that can cast heal and use robots.
0 deaths, I don't remember if there was a difficulty selection, but I would have chosen normal if there was one.
Probably the best feature was trying out the different classes.  Having a nice mix of the classes is fun.
